summary: End-to-end testing of the new Forgot/Reset Password flow on SA Coparents. All 7 backend pytest cases pass (request, preview, confirm, suspended-user privacy, rate limit, used-token rejection, old-password invalidation). All 4 frontend flows pass: login Forgot link, /forgot-password success state, /reset-password error states (no token + bogus token), and the full happy path (valid token -> form -> mismatch toast -> matching passwords -> auto-signed-in to /dashboard, /api/auth/me returns user, session persists across reload). parent1@test.com password has been restored to TestPass123!.
critical_code_review_comments: Backend privacy: the request endpoint returns sent:true for real users and sent:false for unknown/suspended. The boolean technically leaks account existence to a network observer even though the human-readable `message` is identical. Consider always returning sent:true (or omitting the boolean) to fully prevent enumeration. Current behavior is acceptable since tests asserted the same response shape, but mark as a privacy-hardening follow-up.

Rate limit (MAGIC_LINK_RATE_LIMIT_PER_HOUR=5) is shared between magic-link signup and password-reset because both write into the same magic_links collection keyed by IP. A user who recently used magic-link login may unexpectedly hit 429 when requesting a reset (and vice versa). Consider separating counters by `mode`.

On suspended-user path, no `magic_links` row is inserted, so the request still counts toward rate-limit budget only on the success path. That is fine, but the 'pretend we sent it' branch returns `sent: False`, which differs from the unknown-email branch shape — see privacy bullet above.

Frontend ResetPassword.jsx submits without disabling Enter-key form submission while still validating; minor — the form already guards <8 chars and mismatch. No bug, just note that the email field is shown as plain text but is not actually rendered as an input — the spec said 'pre-fills the email read-only'. Implementation displays it inside a <span>, which satisfies the intent but isn't a real disabled input. Acceptable.

Frontend success path redirects to /dashboard but on a reload the AuthContext routes the user to /orientation because the user has not completed orientation. That is existing behavior, not a regression, but flag for awareness.
test_credentials: parent1@test.com / TestPass123! (restored at end of run)
seed_data_creation: Created and deleted a transient suspended user (test_susp_*@test.com) via Mongo to verify privacy of the suspended path. All magic_links rows were cleared between tests to keep rate-limit state deterministic; final cleanup also clears magic_links.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend tests live in /app/backend/tests/test_password_reset.py. They depend on Mongo access (read MONGO_URL/DB_NAME from /app/backend/.env) to clear magic_links between cases (the per-IP rate limit otherwise leaks state). Token extraction relies on the line 'Password reset requested but SMTP not configured. Link for <email>: <url>' being present in /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log or backend.out.log — that is the SMTP-fallback path. If SMTP ever gets configured, switch token extraction to a test-only DB read.
rca of the issue: N/A — no failing tests after rate-limit-state cleanup between tests.
